title: The Sharp Protocol
premise: Vesper Whitlock, a fixer for the Meridian Office—an embassy that exists on no map—has spent three years unable to sleep through the night since a botched extraction in Riga. When a burner phone rings with the voice of her dead handler, Elias, she learns the Office's training program, the Sharp Protocol, never ended: it simply went private, selling its graduates to the highest bidder. Following the phone's breadcrumbs through Vienna, Tallinn, and a decommissioned listening post in the Carpathians, Vesper discovers Elias faked his death to build a kill list of every Protocol asset—and that her own insomnia is a planted conditioning trigger meant to make her the Protocol's perfect weapon. In the end she must choose between burning the network and becoming its final instrument, and she does both: she triggers the kill list, then walks into the sea at Riga, finally sleeping.
about_author: Jonah Montrose is the pen name of a former diplomatic security consultant who spent a decade in posts he still cannot name. He writes thrillers from a farmhouse in Wales, where he claims the silence is load-bearing.

chapters.title: The Number That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Cleaning up a diplomat's indiscretion in Vienna, Vesper runs on four hours' sleep and muscle memory. A burner phone left in her coat pocket rings; the voice is Elias, dead three years. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into hunger—the first real feeling since Riga.

chapters.title: Meridian Rules
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She reports the phone to her superior, Deputy Director Ansel Croft, who orders it destroyed unread. Instead she copies the SIM. Flashback fragments of Riga surface. Emotional beat: the first crack in her institutional loyalty.

chapters.title: Voice from the Cold
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. On a night tram, she calls back. Elias gives her one word—'Kestrel'—and coordinates in Tallinn before the line dies. Someone is following her; she loses them using Protocol tradecraft she was told was retired. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into paranoia.

chapters.title: Tallinn, Off the Books
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. In Tallinn she finds Kestrel, a former Protocol instructor running a maritime salvage front, who confirms the program went private after 'officially' ending—and that Elias was its architect. Emotional beat: betrayal; the training that saved her tonight was built by the man she mourns.

chapters.title: The Graduates
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel explains the Sharp Protocol's true product: not spies but sleepless weapons, conditioned via trauma anchors. He gives her a partial roster of sold assets. Emotional beat: grief for what she is, and cold resolve.

chapters.title: Croft's Quiet Call
chapters.summary: Croft's POV. Croft learns Vesper contacted Kestrel and activates a cleanup team, revealing to the reader he answers to the private buyers, not the state. Emotional beat: bureaucratic menace—he tells himself it's triage, not murder.

chapters.title: Anchor Points
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Decoding Elias's message, Vesper realizes her insomnia isn't trauma—it's an open channel, a conditioning trigger awaiting activation. She tests herself against the trigger and barely holds. Emotional beat: horror at being a loaded gun someone else keeps.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Buried
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She traces Elias's fake death to a clinic outside Gdańsk and finds his living quarters: walls of photographs, including her, annotated for years. Emotional beat: tenderness and violation tangled together—she was watched over, and used.

chapters.title: Interference Pattern
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The cleanup team closes in; Kestrel is taken while Vesper escapes through the shipyards. A stranger named Ilse, another graduate, saves her, recognizing the sleeplessness instantly. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt and the shock of kinship.

chapters.title: What Ilse Knows
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse reveals the buyers convene in ten days at a Carpathian listening post to auction the Protocol itself—methodology, roster, and all. Her own anchor is nearly spent; she has weeks. Emotional beat: urgency as mortality.

chapters.title: The Kill List
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Elias's hidden drive surfaces: not just names but a dead-man's switch he built the network around—the kill list can only be armed by a live graduate's biometric anchor. His plan always required her. Emotional beat: fury that even his love was architecture.

chapters.title: Sleep, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Croft's team captures Vesper and attempts remote activation of her anchor. She resists by deliberately reliving Riga in full memory, reclaiming the trauma instead of being driven by it. Emotional beat: the book's thematic hinge—memory owned, not suffered.

chapters.title: Riga, Revisited
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, extended flashback. The full truth of the incident: the extraction failed because the Office sold her team's route to test buyer interest. Elias helped her survive and then erased himself to build the list. Emotional beat: catharsis; the insomnia finally has a story she can hold.

chapters.title: A Bargain with Ghosts
chapters.summary: Vesper and Ilse's POV. Escaping custody together, they agree on the plan: reach the listening post, arm the kill list, burn everything—including themselves if necessary. Emotional beat: grim partnership, two weapons choosing their own targets.

chapters.title: The Long Road Up
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The journey into the Carpathians; a near-miss at a border crossing forces them to trust a retired asset from the roster who owes Elias. Emotional beat: fragile hope—the network contains people worth saving.

chapters.title: The Listening Post
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Infiltration of the decommissioned station, now a luxury redoubt. She sees the buyers—corporates, a minister, a general—and hears the Protocol described as a product line. Emotional beat: cold clarity about power's appetite.

chapters.title: Croft's Confession
chapters.summary: Croft's POV. Confronted by Vesper inside the post, Croft argues he kept the machine fed so it wouldn't eat more people like her. She doesn't forgive him, but understands him, which is worse. Emotional beat: pity without mercy.

chapters.title: Activation
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The buyers attempt to demonstrate the Protocol live—on her. Under full trigger pressure, Vesper turns the conditioning inward, using the anchor to arm Elias's kill list instead of obeying. Emotional beat: climax; the weapon chooses.

chapters.title: Everything Burns Downward
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The kill list executes across three continents in minutes; the post goes dark as assets turn on their owners. Ilse spends her last strength covering Vesper's exit. Emotional beat: terrible triumph, paid for in full.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Aftermath: Croft dead by his own hand or someone else's; the Office quietly dissolved upward into nothing. Vesper holds evidence that could rebuild the network—or end it publicly—and burns it. Emotional beat: exhaustion and release.

chapters.title: Elias's Last Letter
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A delayed message from Elias unlocks: an apology, an explanation, and permission—to stop carrying him. She reads it on the shore at Riga where it began. Emotional beat: mourning completed at last.

chapters.title: First Sleep
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She walks into the cold Baltic surf—not to die, but to feel something chosen. That night, in a rented room with no burner phones, she sleeps through until morning. Final line lands the theme: memory kept, power refused, rest earned. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace.
